description: Project-specific testing standards for master-model-maven — BDD behaviour testing (capability → BDD .feature → test → evidence), contract-first assertions, real-endpoint integration over mocks, reproducibility, fixture hygiene, stable selectors, production-shaped fixtures. Checked by the pr-reviewer agent against test code in every diff.

standards.title: Do not mock what you can hit directly
standards.description: Integration and end-to-end tests exercise the real dependency the test tier can reach, rather than a stub of it; mock doubles are reserved for pure unit tests of logic with no reachable dependency. In this project, edge-function/integration tests call real Supabase endpoints (ephemeral for pre-merge, shared-staging for regression, production for live).
standards.rationale: Mocking a reachable endpoint tests the mock, not the contract. Source: docs/product/_testing/01-overview.md §1.4.
acceptance_criteria: Integration/E2E tests in the diff call the real dependency the tier provisions rather than stubbing it.
Mock doubles introduced in the diff are confined to pure-unit tests of logic with no reachable dependency.
No diff adds a hand-rolled stub for an endpoint/service the test tier can reach directly (e.g. a Supabase table/function).
anti_patterns: Mocking `supabase.from(...)` in an edge-function integration test that runs against an ephemeral DB.
A fake HTTP layer standing in for a real endpoint the tier already provisions.

standards.title: Tests pin observable contracts, not implementation detail
standards.description: Tests assert observable behaviour — status codes, response shapes, redirects, authorization outcomes — not internal implementation. A refactor that preserves the contract must not require test changes. Do not write tests that assert framework behaviour (React, Radix, Supabase client libraries are trusted dependencies).
standards.rationale: Contract-first tests survive refactors and catch real regressions; implementation-coupled tests are churn. Source: docs/product/_testing/01-overview.md §1.1 and §1.4.
acceptance_criteria: New tests in the diff assert observable outputs (status, response shape, redirect, authorization result), not private internals.
No test in the diff asserts behaviour owned by React/Radix/Supabase client libraries.
Tests in the diff would still pass after a contract-preserving refactor of the unit under test.
anti_patterns: Asserting on a component's internal state variable instead of rendered output.
A test that re-verifies that Radix opens a dialog (framework behaviour).

standards.title: Tests are reproducible locally
standards.description: Any CI failure must reproduce locally with a documented command. Tests must not depend on CI-only state, ordering, or wall-clock; no 'only fails in CI' mysteries.
standards.rationale: Reproducibility is a testing principle; non-reproducible failures cannot be diagnosed or fixed reliably. Source: docs/product/_testing/01-overview.md §1.1.
acceptance_criteria: New tests in the diff run deterministically given a documented local command.
Tests in the diff do not depend on execution order, ambient CI environment, or real current time without a fixed/injected clock.
Any environment a test needs is provisioned by the test or documented, not assumed to exist only in CI.
anti_patterns: A test that passes locally only because of leftover state from a previous test.
Asserting against `Date.now()` without a controlled clock.

standards.title: Each test seeds and cleans up its own fixtures; shared live data is read-only
standards.description: Every test seeds its own fixtures and either cleans them up or uses idempotent guards. Shared live data is treated as read-only and must not be mutated by a test.
standards.rationale: Self-contained fixtures keep tests isolated and re-runnable; mutating shared data causes cross-test interference and pollutes live environments. Source: docs/product/_testing/01-overview.md §1.6.
acceptance_criteria: New tests in the diff create the data they need and remove it (or use idempotent upsert/guard) rather than relying on pre-existing rows.
No test in the diff writes to or deletes shared/live data it did not create.
Authenticated tests in the diff use the designated test identities (TEST_USER_EMAIL/TEST_USER_PASSWORD or the restricted-group/synthetic users), not arbitrary real accounts.
anti_patterns: A test that depends on a specific row already existing in a shared database.
A test that updates a shared fixture and leaves it mutated for the next test.

standards.title: Prefer stable selectors and named timeout constants
standards.description: E2E/component tests select elements by stable, semantic locators — role, label/placeholder, or data-testid — never brittle CSS/nth-child paths. Timeouts use named constants, not inline numeric literals. The project's data-testid contract is STD-TEST-009.
standards.rationale: Stable, conventional selectors and named timeouts keep the suite resilient and readable; brittle CSS selectors and magic-number timeouts cause flake and churn. Source: docs/product/_testing/01-overview.md §1.6.
acceptance_criteria: New tests in the diff select by role, label/placeholder, or data-testid, not brittle CSS or nth-child paths.
Timeouts in the diff reference named constants, not inline numeric literals.
anti_patterns: `page.locator('div > button:nth-child(3)')` instead of a role/test-id selector.
`await expect(...).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15000 })` with an inline literal instead of a named constant.

standards.title: Fixtures must mirror the production data shape
standards.description: Mock fixtures and test doubles return the same shape production returns; a green test on a fixture whose shape differs from production does not constitute coverage of the production path. In this project, entityCrud reads return Display-ID strings (e.g. 'SUB00000001'), not raw integers — fixtures must match.
standards.rationale: If a fixture's shape differs from production (e.g. raw integers vs enriched Display-ID strings), the production path is untested and CI is green on a real break. Source: CLAUDE.md §Defensive Programmer Review ('Green CI ≠ covered').
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures in the diff return the same shape as production for the path under test (e.g. Display-ID strings for PK/FK fields from entityCrud, matching enrichRecords output).
No new fixture in the diff returns a raw integer where production returns a Display-ID string (or vice-versa).
A test covering a Display-ID-sensitive path uses a fixture whose shape matches the enriched production body.
anti_patterns: A fixture returning `{ submission_id: 1 }` for a path that, in production, receives `{ submission_id: 'SUB00000001' }`.
Relying on integer-keyed fixtures to 'prove' a Display-ID parsing path works.
standards.source: Migrated from CLAUDE.md — Defensive Programmer Review checklist ('Green CI ≠ covered')

standards.title: Behaviour tests realise the BDD .feature (no automation without a spec)
standards.description: Testing-side facet of the BDD lifecycle (STD-PROC-008). Behaviour/E2E tests — both API/edge-function and web, but not pure unit tests — realise an authoritative BDD .feature (Gherkin, generated from a capability, STD-PROC-013). The test code (step definitions, playwright-bdd) realises that spec and is never the source of truth. Do not hand-write or auto-scaffold automation divorced from a BDD .feature; every automated behaviour test traces back to a .feature and its capability.
standards.rationale: Realising tests from a capability-generated BDD .feature keeps automation traceable to product intent and prevents drift between intent and tests. Source: docs/_process/04_ai-agile-implementation.md; MAOS BDD Specification.
acceptance_criteria: A behaviour/E2E test added in the diff realises a BDD .feature that traces to a capability (STD-PROC-013).
The test code realises the .feature; the .feature is the authoritative testable spec, not the test code.
The diff does not auto-scaffold or hand-write E2E automation with no corresponding BDD .feature; pure unit tests are exempt.
anti_patterns: Committing automation for a feature with no BDD .feature / capability behind it.
Treating a test/step-definition as the source of truth instead of the .feature.
Auto-generating E2E specs divorced from a capability.

standards.title: Write idempotent CRUD/E2E tests
standards.description: CRUD and E2E tests must be idempotent so re-runs do not fail on unique-constraint violations: before creating a record, check whether it already exists (from a previous run) and, if so, verify and pass rather than re-creating. Tests clean up or use idempotent guards.
standards.rationale: The suite runs repeatedly (scheduled and on PRs) against shared environments; non-idempotent create steps fail on the second run. Source: docs/LOVABLE_KNOWLEDGE.md §8 (Writing Idempotent CRUD Tests).
acceptance_criteria: Create-flow tests in the diff check for the record's existence before creating and short-circuit to verification if present.
Tests in the diff do not assume a clean database and do not fail on re-run due to unique constraints.
Test data created in the diff is cleaned up or guarded so repeated runs stay green.
anti_patterns: A test that always creates `code = 'TEST'` and fails the second run on a unique violation.
Assuming an empty table at the start of an E2E create scenario.
standards.source: Migrated from docs/LOVABLE_KNOWLEDGE.md §8 — Writing Idempotent CRUD Tests

standards.title: Use the EntityRegistry-derived test-ID contract and scope to the active dialog
standards.description: Tests select UI via the stable data-testid contract derived from EntityRegistry naming: dialog-{entityType}, field-{field.name}, save-{entityType}, save-add-{entityType}. Locators are scoped to the active dialog (getByTestId('dialog-...')), not selected globally. Prefer test IDs over fragile role/text/CSS selectors.
standards.rationale: The schema-driven form generator emits these stable IDs; using them (scoped to the dialog) yields resilient tests, while global role/text selectors match multiple elements and flake. Source: docs/LOVABLE_KNOWLEDGE.md §8 (Test-ID Contract / Dialog Handling).
acceptance_criteria: New tests in the diff target dialogs/fields/save controls via dialog-{entityType}/field-{name}/save-{entityType} test IDs.
Form interactions in the diff are scoped to the active dialog locator, not selected from the whole page.
New tests in the diff avoid fragile nth-child/role-last/placeholder-global selectors when a test ID exists.
anti_patterns: `page.getByRole('dialog').last()` instead of `page.getByTestId('dialog-concepts')`.
`page.getByRole('button', { name: /save/i })` matching multiple unscoped buttons.
standards.source: Migrated from docs/LOVABLE_KNOWLEDGE.md §8 — Test-ID Contract Pattern

standards.title: Test artefacts live in their canonical locations; the BDD .feature is the testable spec
standards.description: Test artefacts have a single home. BDD specifications are Gherkin .feature under tests/features/playwright/ (web E2E) and tests/features/deno/ (API/edge), each generated from a capability (STD-PROC-013) and the authoritative testable spec. Step definitions live in tests/step-definitions/*.steps.ts (per the playwright-bdd config); shared fixtures in tests/fixtures/. Pure unit/component tests are not BDD: frontend units are colocated in src/**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,tsx} (Vitest); edge-function unit tests are deno tests beside the function or _shared.
standards.rationale: A single home for behaviour specs, each linked to a capability, keeps the suite discoverable and the playwright-bdd wiring valid; a source-of-truth-in-test-code artefact breaks traceability. Source: playwright.config.ts (defineBddConfig); vitest.config.ts; MAOS BDD Specification.
acceptance_criteria: BDD .feature specs in the diff live under tests/features/playwright/ (web) or tests/features/deno/ (API/edge), each linked to a capability.
Step definitions in the diff live in tests/step-definitions/*.steps.ts; fixtures in tests/fixtures/.
Frontend unit/component tests in the diff are colocated in src/** as *.{test,spec}.{ts,tsx}; edge-function unit tests are deno tests beside the function or _shared.
New E2E behaviour in the diff is a BDD .feature (+ step definition) linked to a capability, not an ad-hoc .spec.ts.
anti_patterns: A BDD .feature with no linked capability.
Adding a .feature outside tests/features/ where the playwright-bdd config will not pick it up.
A standalone Playwright .spec.ts E2E divorced from the BDD structure.
standards.source: Derived from playwright.config.ts / vitest.config.ts; MAOS BDD Specification
